findings.code_context: canonicalGeneratedIdentifier() removes numeric suffixes from every generated JavaScript identifier before dependency and helper digests are compared.
findings.analysis: The normalization is intended to absorb esbuild hygienic renaming, but it is broader than a namespace-specific mapping. A post-publication mutation that renames generated identifiers by adding or removing the accepted numeric suffix, while updating references consistently, can produce the same canonical digest. The exact bundle digest and authenticated package closure reduce exposure, but the canonical provenance comparison no longer distinguishes every generated-code mutation.
findings.exploit_scenario: An actor able to rewrite a staged or reused bundle changes a generated dependency binding such as a2 to a3 and updates its references. The canonical dependency/helper digest remains unchanged, so this particular mutation is not detected by the provenance comparison.
findings.threat_model_reference: Section 5.2 - Generated helper or namespace forgery
existing_mitigations: The pinned dependency closure is checked against an exact trusted integrity digest before semantic exemption.
The published bundle also carries a bundle digest and coherent generation metadata.
Generated helper structure, namespace export call count, mutation analysis, and entry boundary are validated.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the global suffix-stripping rule with a compiler-recorded, namespace-scoped mapping of the exact hygienic aliases emitted by the trusted esbuild build, or compare a canonical AST that preserves all non-hygiene identifier edits.
findings.reasoning: The mutation requires write access to published artifacts and consistent reference updates, and other generation checks may detect it. The canonicalizer nevertheless intentionally erases a class of identifier changes before integrity comparison.
